findings.title: Open TCP port 22 (ssh)
findings.severity_rationale: Open port exposure alone is not an exploitable vulnerability.
findings.description: The SSH service port is open and accessible from the network.
findings.remediation: Restrict SSH access to authorized management networks using network ACLs or host-based firewall rules.
findings.evidence: 22/tcp open  ssh     OpenSSH 6.6.1p1 Ubuntu 2ubuntu2.13 (Ubuntu Linux; protocol 2.0)

findings.title: Missing HTTP Security Headers (http-missing-security-headers)
findings.severity_rationale: Absence of defensive HTTP response headers increases client vulnerability to clickjacking, MIME-sniffing, and cross-site content injection.
findings.description: The server response lacks recommended defensive headers including Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, and X-Frame-Options.
findings.remediation: Configure web server to return Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, and Strict-Transport-Security headers.

findings.title: Filtered HTTP port (80/tcp)
findings.severity_rationale: Filtered state indicates packet filtering or upstream firewall, not a confirmed vulnerability.
findings.description: Port did not respond to TCP SYN packets; network firewalling or packet filtering suspected.
findings.remediation: Verify firewall rules and intended network boundary policy.
